speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what assessment the Government has made of structural unemployment risks facing Singaporean professionals, managers, executives, and technicians (PMETs) in their 40s and 50s; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider further strengthening current measures to support re-employment, mid-career transitions and wage sustainability for this group; and (b) if so, what measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: However, rapid technological change and shifts in the external economic environment mean that our workers should regularly upskill to stay up-to-date with industry needs and remain open to new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This could be more challenging for mature workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government has hence been strengthening measures to support this group to strengthen their career resilience and to manage career transitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We have invested strongly in developing our local workforce and several of our programmes offer a higher level of support for mature workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Those who require a more substantive skills reboot can tap on SSG’s SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme.
In order to improve access to new opportunities, we need to go more upstream.
Workers need to take charge of their career health and take proactive steps to improve their employability.

To support them to navigate the labour market and make longer-term career plans, we have introduced digital tools and services, such as the Careers and Skills Passport, CareersFinder and career guidance programmes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My supplementary question, Sir, is born out of what I think is a perceived gap where PMETs, in particular, engineers and information technology (IT) people, have given me feedback on my home visits and Meet-the-People Sessions that they are finding it extremely difficult to find alternative jobs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I am wondering whether we can look beyond the SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second supplementary question is, to look at mentorship programmes and lateral hires within the industry; that is my second supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And a third supplementary question, which brings it altogether, is the experience that I have with the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union (FDAWU).

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And in the FDAWU, we care for hotels, food and beverage (F&B), retail and restaurants.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And if there is any dip in employment in one sector, then it is a very natural shift to go into another sector, because a person who has worked in a restaurant can then work in a hotel restaurant.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, are we looking at creating tight labour markets within the IT and engineering sectors, such that if there is retrenchment, there can be lateral movements within, for example, union membership, where the unions represent multiple related industries.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I appreciate the good work that the Senior Minister of State and his team are doing, but I am just here trying to propose positive steps to plug the gap where the IT and the engineering sector is concerned; and this is born out of my home visits.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The first supplementary question has to do with plugging the gaps.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The second supplementary question has to do with lateral movements within one union structure.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, if a union represents multiple industries that are actually related, and I think engineering and IT are quite related, can we create a tight labour market within that union structure, so that we have lateral employment opportunities given?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And it is arising out of my experience working closely with the FDAWU.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On his first point, whether we can go beyond what SkillsFuture currently does to support PMETs, especially as the Member mentioned, in the engineering and IT sectors where they may face some challenges.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I mentioned in my main reply, we are trying to go more upstream to prevent even a displacement from a job.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because at this stage when they are in their 40s there could be some early skills obsolescence in the midst of this rapid economic change and disruptive technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we believe that if we go upstream, we can do more preventive measures to help them to remain relevant for a longer period of time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, indeed, going beyond just acquiring skills, how can we build a better career and employment ecosystem to better support them?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Currently, we see that for more higher-end PMEs who are, perhaps, usually head-hunted – rather than them going and applying for a job, people come looking for them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we are thinking about whether some of these services can be something that can be more broadly available for PMEs who may want to avail themselves to other opportunities, even while they are still in employment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And that can apply to many other sectors, not just in engineering and IT.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, that stream of work will continue to see how we can go beyond SkillsFuture, as it currently is today.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And that is what the NTUC has been doing all this while, something that we will continue to support and encourage as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But on the aspect of just trying to facilitate that, I do not think keeping a tight labour market per se, is perhaps, the most appropriate tool to do that.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The labour market is tight not because we want to facilitate lateral movements, but it is tight because we have resource constraints in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I hope that gives the Member a sense of what we are doing at the national level, but also in conjunction with what the union is doing already on the ground.
